title: Integrative Approaches for the Study of the Fluidic Cellular Microenvironment
text:
RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
This proposal is relevant to public health because it addresses critical shortcomings of currently available
methods for studying the relationship between cells and their microenvironment. The development of the
proposed molecular, microfluidic, and computational tools will advance understanding of the role of fluid transport
in regulating biological processes. In addition to laying the foundation for studying disease mechanisms that are
not well captured by current model systems, the results of this work will inform the development of interventional
approaches for the myriad diseases in which pathologic fluid transport plays a role, including cardiovascular
disease and cancer.

title: Cellular signaling mechanisms that drive persistent hyperexcitability in nociceptors
text:
This joint project will define mechanisms in injury-detecting sensory neurons that contribute to life-long
chronic pain after spinal cord and surgical injury. It follows up on discoveries that spinal cord injury causes
a large number of these sensory neurons to change from their normal state of electrical silence into a
persistent state of spontaneous activity with reduced responsiveness to opioids. We now test novel
targets for reversing the spontaneous activity and resistance to opioids for treating reappearing surgical
pain and chronic pain after spinal cord injury.

title: JHU-Mayo-NIA Murine Senescence Mapping Program (JMN-MSMP)
text:
Project Narrative.
Senescent vascular cells contribute to inflammation, fibrosis, and functional decline across many organs during
aging, but their identities and tissue-specific behaviors are poorly defined. This project will identify and validate
vascular senescent cell phenotypes across multiple tissues and determine how these tissue-resident cells relate
to blood-based secreted protein signatures. The results will enable improved biomarkers and inform strategies
to monitor and target harmful senescent cell states in age-related disease.

title: Identify new regulators of outer membrane vesicle entry into macrophages
text:
This project is expected to identify factors required for the entry of outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) of Gram-
negative bacteria into macrophages. The findings will expand our knowledge of bacterial infection and innate
immunity, and will facilitate the development of safer and more effective strategies to combat bacterial
infection and inflammatory diseases.

title: Novel Pathogenic Mechanisms of Joubert Syndrome
text:
Retinal degeneration is a leading cause of blindness. We have discovered a novel link between mitochondrial
defects and disrupted cellular cilia in Joubert syndrome, a rare form of retinal degeneration in children. The
proposed studies will restore the function of mitochondria and cilia; we anticipate that they will lead to new
therapeutics for this blinding disease and for other more common forms of retinal degeneration.

title: Apical extracellular matrix during organ formation
text:
Making a three-dimensional tube is a fundamental process in formation of many organs, including lungs,
kidneys, and digestive organs. We aim to understand the molecular mechanisms of how the apical
extracellular matrix regulates tube dimensions in the Drosophila (fruit fly) salivary gland, a relatively
simple but genetically powerful system. Our work will provide us with insights into understanding the
regulatory mechanisms of normal organ development and human disorders linked to the malformation of
a tube.

title: Analytical Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrum Core (ALC)
text:
RELAVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH | ANALYTICAL LCMS CORE
The projects of the UCLA SCORE renewal will investigate why females with IBS are more susceptible to
gastrointestinal and extraintestinal comorbidity than males with IBS. The Analytical LCMS Core will support
these investigations by providing state-of-the-art determination of estrogen and androgen levels in the
circulation. The core will also determine the levels of sex hormones present in the gut that have been
reactivated by gut microbiota, while evaluating the effects of sex and disease on gut microbial reactivation
enzymes.

title: Understanding the role of RAMS11 in non small cell lung cancer
text:
Lung cancer research has primarily focused on the deregulation of protein-coding genes to identify oncogenes
and tumor suppressors as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets, thereby under-representing the emerging
roles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). Our proposal focuses on how our recently discovered lncRNA,
RAMS11, confers NRF2-dependent oncogenic phenotypes in NRF2/KEAP1 mutant NSCLC lung cancer
patients. A better understanding of how this lncRNA functions could lead to the development of specific
treatments to improve patient outcomes.

title: Biochemical and functional characterization of a novel anti-inflammatory biogenic amine
text:
The major long-term goal of our study is to determine the biological relevance of a novel metabolite (3HKA) of
the tryptophan metabolism, in immunological tolerance. Our data indicate that this metabolite has
immunosuppressive capability in animal models of Psoriasis and SLE reducing the clinical, biochemical, and
immunological signatures of the disease. As such, we propose to therapeutically develop 3HKA as an additional
drug to treat autoimmune diseases.

title: Immune Airway-Epithelial Interactions in Steroid-Refractory Severe Asthma
text:
Severe asthma (SA) is complex, multifactorial and refractory to treatment by corticosteroids (CS). In recent
years, some progress has been made in its treatment with the advent of biologics. Using state-of-the-art
immunological and molecular multi-omics approaches the projects and cores working synergistically will
establish new concepts in immune-epithelial interactions underlying asthma pathogenesis. It is anticipated that
the effector pathways identified in SA in this study can be ultimately targeted to limit disease morbidity.

title: The Role of Mechanosensitive Ion Channels in Glaucoma
text:
Glaucoma is a progressive, blinding disease for which intraocular pressure is the most significant risk factor,
and yet, the mechanisms of how the eye senses pressure remain largely unknown. This project will investigate
the role of mechanosensitive ion channels in glaucoma, and how human variants in mechanosensitive ion
channel genes may be associated with glaucoma risk. These studies will provide fundamental insights into the
mechanosensitive responses of retinal cells at the molecular and physiological level and will lay the foundation
for the development of new neuroprotective therapies for glaucoma.

title: Exploring embryonic exposure to hypoxia as a priming cue for postnatal epidermal insult
text:
While similarities between development and disease have long been appreciated, the ability of embryonic
experiences to shape inflammatory responses remains largely unexplored. Given that barrier tissue stem cells
can accumulate memories of past experiences to modulate cell behavior, I will investigate whether HIF1α activity
in the hypoxic environment of the womb primes the developing skin to react swiftly when faced with later-life
hypoxic experiences of inflammation and tissue injury. Uncovering links between developmental pathways and
later inflammation could reveal new insights into origins of chronic diseases, early diagnostics, and therapeutic
avenues.

title: IgSF11 Signaling Controls Osteoclast Maturation and Pathogenic Bone Loss
text:
Osteoclasts are critical cells for resorbing bone under homeostatic conditions but that also contribute to
pathogenic bone loss under inflammatory conditions. Regulation of osteoclast maturation by externally-
triggered metabolic switching may represent an important avenue for disease mitigation that require further
study.

title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy – The Black/White Disparity
text: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are a leading contributor to maternal mortality in the US, and Black women are three to four times more likely than White women to die from HDP. This study addresses an urgent public health issue by investigating individual, interpersonal, and neighborhood factors that may contribute to differences in HDP outcomes. Results from this research will help guide the development of targeted interventions to improve maternal health, particularly among Black women.

title: Volumetric histopathology of surgical specimens: scalable 3D analysis in breast and prostate cancer
text:
This project will develop a clinically compatible platform for comprehensive three-dimensional pathology of
breast and prostate cancer using tissue clearing, high-throughput two-photon microscopy, and machine-
learning-based analysis. By examining much more of each specimen than current 2-D sampling, the approach
aims to improve assessment of surgical margins and other features linked to cancer recurrence. This added
information may help clinicians make more informed decisions about adjuvant therapy and surveillance.

title: Impacts of copy number variation on gene regulatory networks and fitness in Candida
text:
Pathogenic yeast that are resistant to antifungal drugs are a serious public health concern. To combat the
evolution of drug resistance we need to understand the mechanisms by which copy number variants produce
resistance and the pleiotropic effects they have on fitness and gene expression. Applying high-throughput
CRISPR-based and single-cell sequencing technologies to assay fitness and gene expression across multiple
genetic backgrounds will identify trade-offs that are robust to standing genetic variation and can be exploited
for combination therapy and drug development.

title: Identifying and targeting cancer immune evasion signals against macrophage surveillance
text:
Inducing tumoricidal activities in macrophages represents a promising strategy in cancer immunotherapy. This
study aims to identify and characterize the immune evasion mechanisms employed by cancer cells to escape
macrophage surveillance. Targeting these mechanisms may lead to the development of innovative and effective
macrophage-based cancer immunotherapies.

title: Development of in Vivo Base Editing as a Genetic Treatment for Spinal Muscular Atrophy
text:
Despite all progress in the neuromuscular field,
there is no permanent cure for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA),
and all current available therapies have important limitations. This study will develop strategies to permanently
edit the SMN2 gene to produce full-length Survival Motor Neuron (SMN) protein by applying CRISPR
technologies.
The study will provide pre-clinical evidence towards the development of a lasting single-dose
genetic treatment for SMA.

title: Targeting NLRP3 inflammasome as a therapeutic link between HIV-1 infection and ischemic stroke
text:
(Project Narrative)
The proposed research will investigate NLRP3 inflammasome activation in HIV-1 infection as a driver of stroke
susceptibility. Results from this work will identify molecular pathways linking viral neuroinflammation and stroke
outcome and reveal novel therapeutic targets to reduce stroke burden in people living with HIV.

title: Large Animal Core (Core 1)
text: Large Animal Core Abstract We have developed the first validated, gyrencephalic, large animal model of post- traumatic epilepsy achieving extreme, long-term video EEG digital radiotelemetry, and we have developed cutting-edge technology allowing single cell imaging in the largest species to date. Building on our 5 years’ experience, the Large Animal Core aims to transduce the cortex of swine with or without post-traumatic epilepsy with proteins that report intraneuronal concentrations of chloride and calcium, surgically implant and maintain imaging ports for the Microscopy Core allowing for serial, 2-photon imaging, and produce and archive video/electrographic data and collect and store tissues of swine with or without post-traumatic epilepsy. In particular, the Large Animal Core will provide surgeries (implant the ECoG, AAV injection, install the imaging ports, cortical impact, inject extracellular chloride dye, 2-photon imaging), record video ECoG with real-time analysis, collect tissues, animal husbandry procedures, regulatory compliance, and facilitation of swine housing resources. The Core Director and staff will participate in weekly meetings regarding administrative and scientific matters such as any problem solving any issues that arise, convulsion screening, and presentations of data.
